args.title: Stage 3 requirements for web-calculator
args.description: I inspected the codebase (Stage 1+2 present, no coverage tooling or Docker). Now appending Stage 3 testing/deployment requirements to requirements.md in EARS format.

args.text:
---

## Stage 3 Requirements (Testing Quality, Coverage & Containerization)

The following requirements extend the system per `docs/SEED-3.md` with non-functional goals covering code inspection, comprehensive edge-case testing, measured code-coverage thresholds, and container packaging. All Stage 1 requirements (Requirements 1 through 15) and all Stage 2 requirements (Requirements 16 through 25) remain in force and unchanged. Stage 3 behavior SHALL NOT weaken, remove, or override any Stage 1 or Stage 2 requirement. The current codebase already contains the Stage 1 arithmetic engine and the Stage 2 scientific engine, memory register, and session history; the Stage 3 audit and edge-case testing requirements apply to whichever math operations, state surfaces, and endpoints are actually present in the codebase at the time Stage 3 work begins.

### Glossary Additions (Stage 3)

- **Audit_Log**: A written document, stored in the repository, that records the result of inspecting the Stage 1 and Stage 2 codebase before Stage 3 implementation, including every discovered defect and every category explicitly cleared as having no defect.
- **Coverage_Report**: A machine-generated measurement of statement coverage and branch coverage produced by executing the automated test suite of a repository layer.
- **Coverage_Threshold**: The minimum acceptable coverage value of 80 percent applied independently to statement coverage and to branch coverage for each repository layer.
- **Backend_Coverage_Tool**: The coverage measurement tool integrated with pytest (`pytest-cov`) that produces the backend Coverage_Report.
- **Frontend_Coverage_Tool**: The coverage measurement tool integrated with Vitest (`@vitest/coverage-v8`) that produces the frontend Coverage_Report.
- **Backend_Image**: The container image that packages the Backend_Service for execution.
- **Frontend_Image**: The container image that packages the built Frontend_Client static assets served by a web server.
- **Backend_Dockerfile**: The multi-stage Dockerfile that builds the Backend_Image.
- **Frontend_Dockerfile**: The multi-stage Dockerfile that builds the Frontend_Image using Nginx to serve static assets.
- **Compose_File**: The top-level `docker-compose.yml` file that orchestrates the Backend_Image and Frontend_Image as a multi-container application.
- **Non_Root_User**: An operating-system user account inside a container that is not the `root` user and under which the container's main process runs.

### Requirement 26: Stage 1 and Stage 2 Codebase Audit

**User Story:** As a developer, I want the existing Stage 1 and Stage 2 codebase inspected and its defects documented before Stage 3 changes, so that pre-existing issues are recorded and fixed without regressing baseline behavior.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE System SHALL produce an Audit_Log that records the inspection of the Stage 1 and Stage 2 codebase before any Stage 3 architectural change is applied.
2. THE Audit_Log SHALL cover each of the four inspection categories (functional bug, mathematical inaccuracy, state leakage, and unhandled edge case) either with one or more documented defects or with an explicit record that no defect was found in that category.
3. WHEN a defect is documented in the Audit_Log, THE System SHALL record for that defect the affected component, the input or steps that trigger the defect, and the expected result contrasted with the actual result.
4. THE Audit_Log SHALL record the actual feature set present in the inspected codebase, identifying which Stage 1 and Stage 2 operations, state surfaces, and endpoints exist at the time of inspection.
5. WHEN a documented defect is remediated, THE System SHALL apply the remediation only after the defect is recorded in the Audit_Log.
6. WHEN a documented defect is remediated, THE System SHALL preserve the behavior defined in Requirements 1 through 25 such that every Stage 1 and Stage 2 acceptance criterion continues to hold after remediation.
7. IF a remediation of a documented defect introduces a regression against any acceptance criterion in Requirements 1 through 25, THEN THE System SHALL reject or correct that remediation before the audit activity is considered complete.

### Requirement 27: Backward Compatibility

**User Story:** As a User, I want every existing calculator feature to keep working after Stage 3, so that testing and deployment changes do not break functionality I rely on.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the Stage 3 test and deployment changes are applied, THE Backend_Service SHALL continue to satisfy every acceptance criterion defined in Requirements 1 through 25 that applies to the Backend_Service.
2. WHEN the Stage 3 test and deployment changes are applied, THE Frontend_Client SHALL continue to satisfy every acceptance criterion defined in Requirements 1 through 25 that applies to the Frontend_Client.
3. WHEN the full automated test suite is executed after the Stage 3 changes are applied, THE System SHALL complete the suite with zero test failures and zero errors.

### Requirement 28: Comprehensive Backend Edge-Case Testing

**User Story:** As a developer, I want exhaustive backend edge-case tests, so that critical mathematical and syntactic failure conditions are verified.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE Backend_Service SHALL include pytest tests that assert a division-by-zero expression returns an Error_Response with an HTTP status code in the 4xx range and no calculated result.
2. WHERE a modulo operation is present in the Evaluation_Engine, THE Backend_Service SHALL include a pytest test that asserts a modulo-by-zero expression returns an Error_Response with an HTTP status code in the 4xx range and no calculated result.
3. WHERE the Evaluation_Engine implements inverse trigonometric functions, THE Backend_Service SHALL include pytest tests that assert an `asin` or `acos` applied to an operand whose absolute value exceeds one returns an Error_Response with an HTTP status code in the 4xx range and no calculated result.
4. WHERE the Evaluation_Engine implements logarithm or square-root functions, THE Backend_Service SHALL include pytest tests that assert a logarithm of a non-positive operand and a square root of a negative operand each return an Error_Response with an HTTP status code in the 4xx range and no calculated result.
5. THE Backend_Service SHALL include pytest tests that assert an invalid operator sequence, an unclosed parenthesis, an invalid character, and an empty expression each return an Error_Response with an HTTP status code in the 4xx range and no calculated result.
6. WHEN an arithmetic operation produces a non-finite result through overflow or underflow, THE Backend_Service SHALL include a pytest test that asserts the Backend_Service returns an Error_Response with an HTTP status code in the 4xx range and no calculated result.
7. WHEN the backend edge-case test suite is executed, THE Backend_Service test suite SHALL complete with zero test failures and zero errors.

### Requirement 29: Comprehensive Frontend Component and State Testing

**User Story:** As a developer, I want frontend tests covering input, memory, keyboard, and history, so that UI state behavior is verified.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE Frontend_Client SHALL include Vitest tests that verify expression input handling, asserting that appending and removing characters updates the Expression_Display to the expected content.
2. WHERE the Frontend_Client implements a Memory_Register, THE Frontend_Client SHALL include Vitest tests that verify the memory add, subtract, recall, and clear operations and the Memory_Indicator visibility defined in Requirement 20.
3. THE Frontend_Client SHALL include Vitest tests that verify keyboard event handling for digit, operator, evaluate, backspace, and reset keys as defined in Requirement 10.
4. WHERE the Frontend_Client implements a Calculation_History, THE Frontend_Client SHALL include Vitest tests that verify history rendering, newest-first ordering, entry selection, and clearing as defined in Requirement 21.
5. WHEN the frontend component and state test suite is executed, THE Frontend_Client test suite SHALL complete with zero test failures and zero errors.

### Requirement 30: Code Coverage Threshold

**User Story:** As a developer, I want measured coverage gates on both layers, so that the test suites demonstrably exercise the code.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE Backend_Service test tooling SHALL produce a Coverage_Report that reports both statement coverage and branch coverage using the Backend_Coverage_Tool.
2. THE Frontend_Client test tooling SHALL produce a Coverage_Report that reports both statement coverage and branch coverage using the Frontend_Coverage_Tool.
3. WHEN the Backend_Service test suite is executed with coverage measurement, THE Backend_Service SHALL achieve statement coverage of at least 80 percent and branch coverage of at least 80 percent.
4. WHEN the Frontend_Client test suite is executed with coverage measurement, THE Frontend_Client SHALL achieve statement coverage of at least 80 percent and branch coverage of at least 80 percent.
5. IF the measured statement coverage or branch coverage of the Backend_Service is below the Coverage_Threshold, THEN THE Backend_Service test run SHALL report a failing outcome.
6. IF the measured statement coverage or branch coverage of the Frontend_Client is below the Coverage_Threshold, THEN THE Frontend_Client test run SHALL report a failing outcome.

### Requirement 31: Backend Containerization

**User Story:** As an operator, I want a secure production container image for the backend, so that the Backend_Service can be deployed consistently.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE System SHALL provide a Backend_Dockerfile that uses a multi-stage build to produce the Backend_Image.
2. THE Backend_Dockerfile SHALL base the final image stage on a minimal Python base image.
3. WHEN the Backend_Image runs the Backend_Service process, THE Backend_Image SHALL run that process as a Non_Root_User.
4. WHEN the Backend_Image is started, THE Backend_Image SHALL launch the Backend_Service listening on a configured network port that serves the Evaluate_Endpoint.
5. THE Backend_Dockerfile SHALL install only the runtime dependencies required to run the Backend_Service in the final image stage.

### Requirement 32: Frontend Containerization

**User Story:** As an operator, I want a production container image for the frontend, so that the built client assets are served efficiently.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE System SHALL provide a Frontend_Dockerfile that uses a multi-stage build to compile the Frontend_Client and produce the Frontend_Image.
2. THE Frontend_Dockerfile SHALL serve the compiled static assets of the Frontend_Client using Nginx in the final image stage.
3. WHEN the Frontend_Image receives a request for a client-side route that does not correspond to a static asset file, THE Frontend_Image SHALL return the Frontend_Client entry document so that client-side routing resolves the route.
4. WHEN the Frontend_Image is started, THE Frontend_Image SHALL serve the Frontend_Client on a configured network port.

### Requirement 33: Multi-Container Orchestration

**User Story:** As a developer, I want a single compose file to run the whole app locally, so that the backend and frontend start together with correct wiring.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE System SHALL provide a Compose_File at the repository root that defines a Backend_Service container built from the Backend_Dockerfile and a Frontend_Client container built from the Frontend_Dockerfile.
2. WHEN the Compose_File is brought up, THE System SHALL start both the Backend_Service container and the Frontend_Client container.
3. WHEN the Frontend_Client container forwards a request addressed to the Evaluate_Endpoint, THE Compose_File SHALL route that request to the Backend_Service container over the shared container network.
4. THE Compose_File SHALL map a host network port to the Frontend_Client container so that the Frontend_Client is reachable from the host.
5. WHEN a container defined in the Compose_File exits unexpectedly, THE Compose_File SHALL apply a restart policy that attempts to restart that container.

args.response:
Completed the Requirements phase of the Stage 3 expansion for the existing "web-calculator" feature spec.

Grounding: I inspected the actual codebase first. Findings that shaped the requirements:
- Stage 1 + Stage 2 are BOTH fully present (backend engine has scientific.py + constants.py; frontend has memoryReducer.ts, historyReducer.ts, ScientificKeypad.tsx, AngleModeToggle.tsx, HistoryPanel.tsx, MemoryIndicator.tsx).
- No coverage tooling exists: backend pyproject.toml has pytest + hypothesis but NO pytest-cov and no coverage gate; frontend package.json has Vitest + RTL + MSW but NO @vitest/coverage-v8 and no coverage script.
- Test files are sparse (backend tests/ has only properties/strategies.py; frontend has only smoke.test.tsx).
- No Docker artifacts exist anywhere.

Action: Appended a new "Stage 3 Requirements" section to .kiro/specs/web-calculator/requirements.md via append — all Stage 1 (1-15) and Stage 2 (16-25) content and numbering preserved untouched. Added a Stage 3 glossary and Requirements 26-33 in EARS format:
- R26 Codebase Audit (4 categories: functional bug, mathematical inaccuracy, state leakage, unhandled edge case; document before fixing; no regressions against 1-25; record actual feature set).
- R27 Backward Compatibility (Requirements 1-25 still hold; full suite zero failures).
- R28 Backend Edge-Case Testing (div/modulo by zero, inverse-trig domains, log/sqrt of negatives, invalid syntax, overflow/underflow) — modulo and scientific cases gated with WHERE since they depend on what's implemented.
- R29 Frontend Component/State Testing (input, memory, keyboard, history) — memory/history gated with WHERE.
- R30 Coverage Threshold (>=80% statement AND branch on both layers; failing run below threshold).
- R31 Backend Containerization (multi-stage Dockerfile, minimal base, non-root, runtime-only deps).
- R32 Frontend Containerization (multi-stage, Nginx, client-side routing fallback).
- R33 Multi-Container Orchestration (root docker-compose.yml wiring both services, API routing, port mapping, restart policy).

The .config.kiro was already correct (requirements-first, feature) so no change was needed.

Per the requirements-first workflow, I stopped after the Requirements phase. The user reviews requirements before the UI advances to the Design phase (next: add Stage 3 design covering the audit report, test strategy/coverage tooling, and Docker/compose architecture).
